Supposedly, my '03 jetta has "lifetime" transmission fluid. I've heard online that you should change it anyways. I've noticed sometimes that my transmission slips. Could this have to do with never changing the fluid?

Heya mvartan!

It's important to note that "lifetime" doesn't mean forever. It's quite the misnomer in the automotive world.

If your mileage is over 150,000, I would absolutely recommend replacing lifetime transmission fluid. Sometimes slipping will result from fluid breaking down over its useful lifetime, and other times it is indicative of clutch packs beginning to wear in your automatic transmission.

You are correct in assuming that your first course of action to attempt to remedy your slipping transmission is changing the fluid. Here's an eHow article for changing the transmission fluid for your specific vehicle!

It's also important to note that an automatic transmission "flush" (as opposed to just draining the old fluid and refilling with new) is a very controversial service in the automotive community. From personal experience, I have found that flushes on high-mileage transmissions have a good chance of destroying the transmission. This is not always the case, but it seems to be a gamble.

Thanks for starting this sub. Given that I know even less about auto repair than I do about neurosurgery (and no, I am not a neurosurgeon) it's nice to have a place for the occasional question. For instance, when driving my hubby's 2006 Civic I noticed a wheezing sound when accelerating. It's not really loud, and performance seems to be fine, but it's definitely a sound that my 2006 Civic doesn't make (yeah, we drive the same car LOL). Does that seem like anything to lose sleep over? Or just have the mechanic check it out next time it's in for an oil change?

Hey dave! Wheezing could be a number of things. I'm afraid I'm the one with the questions now.

Does it sound hollow and drone-like, or does it whistle? Low-pitch, high-pitch, or just the sound of air rushing?

As simple as it sounds, you may be due for an air filter. I'd certainly check yours (or have a shop do it for free!) if you're concerned.

As far as severity, rushing air noises like "wheezing" aren't generally much cause for concern. If you hear rhythmic tapping, or hear a hollow, slightly metallic roar, however, its time to go check it out.

If you'd like to further diagnose the issue, I can run down a couple of things you can do to check into it more.

Thanks for your quick reply! Hmm, how to describe? It's like wind blowing through an open window in your house and the screen on the window makes it have kind of a whistly overtone. The whistly overtone is higher pitched with faster acceleration. It's not overly loud -- with the car windows open, I didn't even hear it -- only when the windows were closed. Definitely no tapping or roaring.

Alrighty. Does the whistle follow the engine RPM, or the speed of the car?

If it goes up and down with the engine RPM, and sounds very faintly metallic (like sharpening a knife), you may have an accessory drive pulley going bad, or I'd suspect the air filter.

If it goes up and down with the speed of the vehicle, you may have a resonance noise caused by an errant plastic underbody tray, or even your windshield wipers! If you have any cosmetic front end or side damage on the car (hypothetically! I'm sure you're a great driver!) that could very well be where your sound is originating from.

At any rate, this does not sound at all like any cause for concern. If it's annoying you enough to want to track it down, you can put painters tape in different channels/valleys/anywhere you'd expect wind to be able to whistle, and see if it goes away. Common spots are the space between the side mirrors and the doors, or the holes in the windshield wipers.

It goes up and down with RPM, but it doesn't sound even faintly metallic to me. I'm not sure when the air filter was last changed, but no more expensive and doable than that endeavor is (I can even change air filters all by myself LOL!) it wouldn't be a bad idea to change both air and cabin filters in both our cars. Will give that a try and see if that changes the wheezing. Thanks so much for your responses!

No problem!

Well that rules out the wind resonance. All signs point to your engine air filter. Other possible causes would be vacuum lines, or a hole or crack in the intake tube.

I just went in to a Chiropractor who took x-rays and it was discovered that one of the little points on my spine is actually connected to my hip bone, and likely has been my entire life. My hips are also tilted so that the left one is almost an inch higher than my right. My doctor didn't really explain what all that means for me, or if it can be really fixed? I had a friend once who said she had something similar, and she was on disability for it. I don't really understand what is going on, how this got this way, and what I need to be doing to help the process. I've been in chronic pain for years and just really want it to stop. :(
One of the points on my Vertebrae is fused to my left hip bone. What does this mean for me?

Without an x-ray it's hard to guess what you are describing. I would guess a sacralization of L5. BUT that is probably not the cause of your pain. This sort of thing happens during development, so you've had it since you were a baby. It is possible that if the sacralization is on one side only, you may have some faulty biomechanics (chiropractic bread and butter). It is a fun find on the x-ray, but it's no reason to be scared. Chiropractic is great for anything dealing with muscles, skeleton, and even nerves. A sacralization of L5 just means you have an extra joint that most people don't have.

Please keep in mind, what I just wrote is all based on the HUGE assumption I made based on the vague description you gave. You are best to ask your chiropractor all these questions. I'm positive they will explain anything you ask.
